label: H. Marshall Chadwell
narrative: H. Marshall Chadwell headed the CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence in 1952 and is the man who moved the UFO problem out of the Air Force and into the intelligence community. After the July 1952 Washington flap he wrote a series of memoranda to the Director of Central Intelligence — 11 September and 2 October 1952 among them — noting that official reports had totalled 250 in July 1952 alone and that 'the flying saucer situation contains two elements of danger which... have national security implications.' The two elements were psychological warfare vulnerability and the saturation of air defence reporting channels. Chadwell proposed a study group to systematise the problem, floating MIT's Project Lincoln and Caltech as venues, and it was Chadwell who, with H. P. Robertson, assembled the January 1953 panel. His own agency's official history states that CIA sponsorship of that panel was forbidden from being mentioned. Chadwell is therefore the origin point of a documented US government decision to treat public belief, rather than the objects, as the thing to be managed.
